events.title: Stephenson's Rocket Wins the Rainhill Trials
events.description: In a famous contest held in Lancashire, England, George and Robert Stephenson's locomotive Rocket beat its rivals. It proved that steam locomotives could haul passengers and freight quickly and reliably.
events.significance: The victory led to Rocket's design being used for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway. That line helped launch the age of railways.

events.title: Korea's Empress Myeongseong Is Assassinated
events.description: Japanese agents and their collaborators broke into Gyeongbokgung Palace in Seoul and killed Empress Myeongseong. She was a strong-willed consort who had resisted growing Japanese influence over Korea.
events.significance: The killing, known as the Eulmi Incident, caused outrage in Korea. It deepened tensions over foreign control of the peninsula in the years before Japan annexed it.

events.title: Germany Annexes Western Poland
events.description: A few weeks after invading Poland, Nazi Germany formally annexed large areas of the country's west. The annexed territory included the Danzig region and the Warthegau.
events.significance: The annexation opened a brutal occupation policy of forced expulsions, colonization and persecution. These measures were among the early steps in the wider horrors of World War II.

events.title: Che Guevara Is Captured in Bolivia
events.description: The Argentine-born revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara was captured by Bolivian forces while leading a guerrilla campaign in the country's remote mountains. He was executed the following day.
events.significance: His death ended his attempt to spread revolution across Latin America. It also made him an enduring and widely debated symbol of rebellion.
